corrected_value.authors: Zhao J, Bradfield JP, Li M, Wang K, Zhang H, Kim CE, et al.
corrected_value.title: The role of obesity-associated loci identified in genome-wide association studies in the determination of pediatric BMI

decisions.quote: The association of the FTO polymorphism (rs8044769) with BMI was not replicated in the Chinese Han population either. The previous studies showed that FTO was associated with BMI [6–12], and two of them referred to rs8044769 as BMI-associated SNP [11, 12]. In the association analysis of rs8044769 with BMI, we found no association between rs8044769 and BMI. And the BMIs corresponding different genotypes of rs8044769 showed no significant difference.
decisions.reason: Prior adjudication and state files are absent for this work. Dai et al. (2018) empirically evaluate the association between FTO SNP rs8044769 and BMI in their Chinese Han sample (Tables 4 and 5) and explicitly state in the Discussion that the rs8044769–BMI association reported specifically in References 11 and 12 was not replicated. Reference 11 is Zhao et al. (2009, Obesity, 10.1038/oby.2009.159), which is an independent original study absent from shipped row 1152 (Zeggini et al., 2012) and distinct from sibling targets 1, 3, and 4.
